From ardh- (“to come”) + -shëm.
According to Çabej, a derivative of harr (“to weed”). Alternatively a back formation of arnoj (“to patch”), borrowed from Latin renovāre (“to renew, restore, revive”).

From Proto-Albanian *baltā (“marsh”), hypothetically from a Proto-Indo-European *bʰolH-to- (“marsh”), originally “the white one”, a derivative of *bʰel- (“shining, white”). Cognate with Proto-Slavic *bolto (“swamp”), Lithuanian báltas (“white, shining”). Often considered an Illyrian substrate word together with Latin blattea. It could also turn out to be a Mediterranean substrate word; compare Italian palta (“swamp”). Borrowed from a South Slavic language, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *besěda (“sitting outside, gathering, conversation”). Compare Old Church Slavonic бесѣда (besěda, “conversation, word”) Serbo-Croatian beseda (“word, speech”), Macedonian беседа (beseda).

From Greek τσιμπίδα (tsimpída), from Albanian cimb.

Uncertain. Either from gardh or a compound of gër- + dhele, derivative of dhe (see also dheul). Alternatively, a compound of gër- + and dhe (“land, land”) + -ele (enlargement suffix).
From Old Albanian kunorë (preserved in Gheg), from Latin corōna (“garland, crown”). The sense marriage derives from Byzantine tradition.

Calque of Serbo-Croatian Gornja Luka. Llukë e Epërme and Llukë e Poshtme were originally one hamlet, attested as Лучане (Lucane), which was plural of Luka. Given the geography, it is most likely from Serbo-Croatian luka (“meadow; arable land”).

ety.text: From dialectal Montenegrin ograđa, compare standard Serbo-Croatian ograda (“fence, enclosure”). Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *o(b)gordъ, a derivative of *gordъ (“settlement, enclosure”).
Borrowed through Vulgar Latin from Latin pinna. Displaced native Albanian perk.

ety.text: Unknown. Maybe from Proto-Albanian *štuop-se, from Proto-Indo-European *st(y)oy-. Compare Old English stān (“stone”).

An Arbëresh word from Calabria, first listed by De Rada. Meyer derives it from lang, lëng, with the ska- prefix where he sees the Greek ξε- (xe-). Çabej accepts the possibility of a relation to cangë instead. Goes with callangur in Vlorë dialect.
Gerund of trashëgoj; trashëgoj + -im.

s.g: A town and municipality in northwestern Albania.

ety.text: Borrowed from South Slavic, from Proto-Slavic *vydra. Doublet of lundër.

ety.text: A methatesized formation from an earlier *vëndër, from Proto-Albanian *ŭ(n)dərā, from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰrom. Compare Old Church Slavonic ведро (vedro, “fine weather”), Old Norse veðr (“wind, air, weather”), Old English weder. Alternatively from Proto-Albanian *awa-raunta, a derivative of rëndë (“heavy”).
